question: Which statement best describes HTML parsing?
options: The browser reads HTML and builds a tree of elements called the DOM. Malformed markup may still render, but the browser can repair it unexpectedly. It is like turning a written outline into a tree of rooms. Semantic elements help browsers and assistive technology understand the structure. For example, a missing closing tag can change the DOM tree the browser constructs. For example, inspect the DOM tree when the browser repairs malformed nesting.

Layout calculates where boxes appear and how large they are. Changing width or font size can move nearby content. It is like rearranging furniture and finding that the walkway changed. Reserve image dimensions and avoid unnecessary layout changes to reduce visible jumps. For example, a newly loaded font can change line breaks and move content below it. For example, reserve image space to prevent text moving when the asset arrives.

Painting turns text, colors, borders, and images into drawing work; compositing combines layers into the final frame. It is like painting separate scenery and combining it into one stage view. Some transform and opacity animations can avoid repeated layout, but profile the actual interaction. For example, a transform animation may avoid recalculating layout for every frame. For example, measure a frame before changing an animation property for performance.

The browser reads CSS and decides which styles apply to each element. It builds style information for the page. It is like choosing the right paint and measurements for each room. Complex selectors and large stylesheets can add work, but measure before assuming they are the bottleneck. For example, a broad CSS selector may match many nodes, but measure before treating it as slow. For example, use computed styles to find the rule that produced the current appearance.

It is like turning a written outline into a tree of rooms. Semantic elements help browsers and assistive technology understand the structure. For example, a missing closing tag can change the DOM tree the browser constructs. For example, inspect the DOM tree when the browser repairs malformed nesting.

For example, a long click handler can make a visible button feel unresponsive. For example, break up a long handler when interaction becomes delayed.
